chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: The Milt Jackson Quartet at Minton's and Newport
summary: The group that became the MJQ began as the Milt Jackson Quartet with Percy Heath and Horace Silver, played the first Newport festival, and swung before John Lewis's subdued style.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Up there at Minton's you formed the --
Yeah, formed the Milt Jackson Quartet, with Percy Heath --
No. No, John was going to the Manhattan School at the time.
You know, after the band broke up, he went to -- back to school.
And so we had -- oh, we had Gildo Mahonas (PHONETIC), whatever his name is, on piano. Then we had Horace Silver.
Oh, yeah. Well, we made the first Newport Jazz Festival, was the MJQ with Horace Silver on piano.
So you and Horace and Percy and Milt.
And Bags, yeah. Yeah, that was the quartet. Then when I went to Minton's we hired Sonny Rollins. So I got -- Sonny was hanging around, not doing much.
So I got Teddy to hire Sonny.
Well, the quartet didn't have that character that it got afterwards.
It didn't have that subdued character.
No, no. It was just straight out swing.
